items.title: Anthropic Hits $2 Trillion in Historic IPO | Altimeter's Four Seasons of AI
items.summary: Altimeter AI Partner Apoorv Agrawal breaks down the historic scale of the AI supercycle—where Big Tech CapEx has hit $860 billion—and explains why Anthropic’s S-1 reveals one of the most capital-efficient, fastest-scaling businesses in history, underpinned by a 1.5T–2T IPO valuation (11–14x forward revenue) and a "Four Seasons of AI" framework led by Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX, and Google.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** Altimeter AI Partner Apoorv Agrawal breaks down the historic scale of the AI supercycle—where Big Tech CapEx has hit $860 billion—and explains why Anthropic’s S-1 reveals one of the most capital-efficient, fastest-scaling businesses in history, underpinned by a 1.5T–2T IPO valuation (11–14x forward revenue) and a "Four Seasons of AI" framework led by Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX, and Google.

## The AI Supercycle & Early-Inning Adoption
* **Historic Capital Expenditure:** Big Tech AI CapEx has reached ~$860 billion this year, having more than tripled over the last two years to rival U.S. defense spending. As a percentage of GDP, this spend already exceeds every major infrastructure boom of the past 100 years (railroads, oil & gas, telco, shale).
* **The AI Stack vs. Cloud Economy:** While the traditional cloud economy generates ~$600B in application/software revenue supported by ~$300B in infra and ~$80B in semis, the AI economy currently generates ~$140B–$150B at the model/app layer on top of a much larger semiconductor base. However, over the last 2–3 years, the AI economy has grown 6x overall while the apps and models layer has grown ~100x.
* **Shift to Agentic AI:** The market has transitioned from "Phase 1" (chatbots/knowledge retrieval, launched with ChatGPT in Nov 2022, making up ~80% of early use cases) to "Phase 2" (agentic AI, long-running agents, and "swarms of agents" for coding, sales, marketing, support, and investment teams, now ~80% of agentic use cases).
* **Widening Adoption Gaps ("A Tale of Two Cities"):**
  * **Enterprise:** OpenAI data shows its top 10% of customers grew usage 17x over the past 1–1.5 years, compared to 2x for the median customer.
  * **Individual:** Cursor data shows the top 10% of users consume two-thirds of all tokens.
  * **Headroom:** Fortune 500 customers spending over $100,000 annually on Anthropic report that it represents less than 0.1% of their total expenses, signaling massive runway as adoption moves from 0.1% toward 1%.

## Anthropic’s S-1 & IPO Valuation
* **Unprecedented Scale & Growth:** Anthropic has grown 10x every year for the last three years, hitting ~$17 billion in Q3 revenue—the fastest scale-up in history.
* **Diversified Enterprise Base:** The company has ~12,000 customers paying over $100,000/year and ~1,900 customers paying over $1 million/year, with 900% net revenue retention and minimal customer concentration.
* **Capital Efficiency & Margins:** Anthropic burned less than $10 billion in cash to reach its ~$17B revenue run rate. The cost to serve $1 of revenue has dropped from $0.88 of compute to $0.15, yielding ~85% margins.
* **Compute Monetization:** Through heterogeneous compute orchestration (TPUs, Trainium, Nvidia GPUs), Anthropic’s compute monetization has risen from ~$16/watt to ~$60/watt.
* **Valuation Thesis:** At the rumored $1.5T–$2T IPO range, Anthropic trades at 11x–14x forward GAAP revenue—a reasonable multiple compared to current market comps.

## The "Four Seasons of AI" & Evergreen Open Source
* **OpenAI:** Now at over 1.2 billion ChatGPT users, OpenAI ended September at a ~$50B revenue run rate (beating year-end guidance). Following a "code red" earlier in the year, it shipped frontier models (Astra) and products (Codex, ChatGPT Work) while upgrading its commercial leadership (Dolly Rojik, Brian McCarthy, Chad Peets).
* **SpaceX (AI Infrastructure):** SpaceX’s ~$60B revenue run rate is now ~50% AI infrastructure (SI unit), ~33% Starlink, and the remainder launch. Its SI unit added over 20% relative market share in Q3.
  * **Spot Compute Model:** Unlike neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius) that lease long-term (1–3 years) at $10–$20/watt, SpaceX rents compute at spot prices ($25–$50/watt, currently at the $50/watt high end), allowing it to recoup CapEx in under a year (vs. 2–3 years for neoclouds).
  * **Scale:** Estimated to end this year at ~3 GW of compute, guiding to ~13 GW by the end of next year.
* **Google ("A Tale of Two Cities"):** While Google Search (~$250B run rate) is growing at 12%, Google Cloud—which houses its TPU business—is at a $120B revenue run rate growing 103% YoY (8x faster than Search), serving customers like Anthropic and Oracle.
* **Open Source (The Evergreen Fifth Season):** Expected to capture 20%–30% of all AI spend, driven by AI-native startups (e.g., Cursor, Instinct, Decagon, Harvey) and enterprises seeking control, lower inference costs, and data sovereignty.
  * Open-source frontier models consistently lag closed frontier models by ~6 months.
  * Value accrues at the inference/cloud layer via platforms like **Baseten**, **Fireworks**, and **Modal** (e.g., OpenAI recently partnered with Baseten so enterprise customers can burn down OpenAI credits on open-source models).

## Data Center Bottlenecks & Market Outlook
* **Power & Permitting Constraints:** The U.S. is expected to end this year at 35–40 GW of compute capacity online. While 40–50 GW of additions were forecasted for next year, permitting and regulation will likely cause a 10–15 GW shortfall.
* **Winners vs. Losers:** Hyperscalers holding large capacity pools benefit as bottlenecks, though their expansion ambitions face risk. Conversely, smaller neoclouds and startups "17th in line" for capacity face existential risk.
* **Who Wins the Stack:** While "everyone is going to win" (chips, data centers, clouds, models), it has so far been a "game of emperors" favoring the largest balance sheets. Over time, improving compute efficiency will allow more value to accrue to the application and startup layers.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **OpenAI Revenue:** OpenAI will generate $140B–$150B in GAAP revenue next year (up from ~$20B–$21B at the end of last year) — *Apoorv Agrawal*
* **SpaceX Revenue & Compute:** SpaceX is guiding to a $100B revenue run rate by the end of this year and $500B–$1T by the end of next year, alongside scaling from ~3 GW of compute this year to ~13 GW by the end of next year — *Apoorv Agrawal (citing SpaceX guidance)*
* **U.S. Compute Shortfall:** Permitting and regulatory bottlenecks will likely cause a 10–15 GW shortfall against the 40–50 GW of U.S. compute capacity additions forecasted for next year — *Apoorv Agrawal*
* **Open Source Market Share:** Open source will capture 20%–30% of all AI spend long-term, with gross margins accruing primarily at the inference layer (Baseten, Fireworks, Modal) — *Apoorv Agrawal*
* **Anthropic IPO Performance:** Anthropic’s IPO (at $1.5T–$2T, or 11–14x forward revenue) will be a "phenomenal short-term success, and certainly long-term," cementing the "private Mag 7" as the leading companies for the next decade and more — *Apoorv Agrawal*

## Notable Quotes
> "Fortune 500 customers that spend more than $100,000 on Anthropic say that it is less than 0.1% of the total expense. We're in inning one of this whole thing... it's going to go from 0.1% of their expenses to 1% and you know, that's how you get the 10x gains." — *Apoorv Agrawal*

> "They burned less than $10 billion of cash [to get to $17B revenue run rate]... Serving a dollar of revenue has gone down from 88 cents of compute to 15 cents. That's why they got 85% margins." — *Apoorv Agrawal*

> "So far, it has been a game of emperors and we've seen the biggest players with the biggest balance sheet win. But... as compute efficiency started to kick in, as models get cheaper, more and more value will accrue at the top of the stack, which is models and applications and new startups." — *Apoorv Agrawal*

> "We thought SpaceX was a space business, but turns out it's an AI business." — *Apoorv Agrawal*

items.title: Huang's Resignation Dissolves the Nvidia AI Vertical Stack | The Weekly Wrap
items.summary: The resignation of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections have triggered a market correction, effectively dissolving Nvidia’s circularly financed "virtual holding company."
items.content_text:
**TL;DR**
The resignation of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections have triggered a market correction, effectively dissolving Nvidia’s circularly financed "virtual holding company." With Nvidia no longer backstopping the AI stack, AI is no longer a single monolithic trade, bringing stock picking and fundamental valuation back to the forefront.

---

## Market Correction & The "Jensen Unwind"
* **Market Action:** From Friday through Thursday (Nov 19), the NASDAQ fell ~4%. The market declined Monday and Tuesday, staged a small rally Wednesday, and saw only a brief, fading pop on Thursday following the Anthropic IPO.
* **Political & Leadership Catalysts:** A Democratic sweep of both houses in the midterms introduced the risk of an AI moratorium or data center construction slowdown. Combined with Jensen Huang’s resignation, these events dwarf all other market news.
* **S&P 500 AI Concentration:** 
  * Infotech represents 40% of the S&P 500; adding tech-adjacent giants like Google and Amazon brings it to 50%.
  * Including utilities, large banks, asset managers/alternative asset managers funding data centers, and industrials providing construction or power (e.g., Eaton, Quanta, GE Vernova) pushes AI-exposed companies to 65% of the S&P 500.
* **Circular Financing & Dissolution:** Under Huang, Nvidia operated as a "virtual vertical holding company" by taking equity stakes or issuing loans to customers who used that capital to buy Nvidia chips—including Anthropic ($20B), OpenAI ($30B), SpaceX ($20B), CoreWeave ($2.5B), and Nebius ($2B).
  * Huang's resignation dissolves this structure. While tech leaders want him back, Treasury Secretary Bessent has appointed himself watchdog, making a front-door return to Nvidia unlikely.
  * Banks, private credit, private equity, and shareholders must now evaluate these AI companies on their own standalone merits (cash flow, balance sheets, leadership, and financing).

## Nvidia’s Earnings & Forward Uncertainty
* **Q3 Results (Backward-Looking):** Nvidia reported EPS of $2.68 (+111% YoY) and revenue of $116B (+103% YoY).
* **Guidance & Stock Reaction:** Management guided next quarter’s revenue to $130B, explicitly excluding "compute revenue from China." The stock rose ~3% after hours, opened up Wednesday, and closed slightly down.
* **Opacity & Red Flags:**
  * Roughly 20% of Nvidia's revenue reportedly came from shipments to "dicey Asian entities" that were likely illegal and could drop to zero.
  * It remains unclear whether Nvidia’s guidance excludes only direct sales to China or also sales to Asian intermediaries funneling chips into China.
  * Eisman argues management made a mistake by issuing guidance at all before unwinding circular financing and quantifying lost revenue.

## How to Think About Quarterly Earnings
* **Earnings Cadence:** Begins ~15 days after quarter-end, opening with the banks and closing ~6 weeks later with Nvidia.
* **Shifting Sector Metrics:**
  * *Banks:* Loan growth, net interest margin (NIM) changes, operating efficiency, and credit quality.
  * *Tech/AI:* Shifted from revenue, earnings, and backlog to CapEx, cash flow, and whether CapEx is funded internally or via capital markets.
  * *Software (SaaS):* Shifted from seat growth and pricing trends to any signs that AI is slowing growth rates.
* **Thesis Checking & Guidance:** Earnings serve as a data-point check (e.g., 16% vs. 14% growth against a 15% thesis). Because companies "under-promise and over-deliver" and can massage accounting within limits, missing guidance signals a potential fundamental issue.
* **The "Steve Eisman Drama Scale" (1–10, Nvidia at 11):** For low-drama stocks like Coca-Cola, backward-looking numbers suffice. When sector narratives shift rapidly (like AI today, or Cisco’s recent strong report), backward-looking earnings tell investors very little about future quarters.

## Retail & Consumer Earnings: Housing Drag vs. Turnarounds
* **Home Depot:** Facing the worst existing home sales market in decades ("a bad macro trumps a good company"). Reported EPS of $3.86 (+3% YoY) and same-store sales comp of +2.2% (50 bps beat), but guided Q4 comps to just 1% (below consensus), sending the stock down Tuesday (roughly flat YTD).
* **Lowe’s:** Reported EPS of $3.10 (+1% YoY) and same-store sales comp of +1.8% (160 bps beat, but still poor).
* **Target:** Turnaround efforts are succeeding, with EPS of $2.65 (+49% YoY) and same-store sales growth of +5.6% (well above expectations).
* **Walmart:** Reported EPS of $0.65 (+5% YoY, a $0.01 beat) and net sales growth of +4.4%. Trading as a "high-class safety stock" amid the post-September 30 AI reversal, shares have climbed from $105 to $125.

## The Anthropic IPO & Mailbag
* **Anthropic IPO:** Went public Thursday (Nov 19) to an anti-climactic reception. Eisman finds the stock uncompelling and is uninvolved due to:
  * *Slowing Growth:* Sequential revenue growth decelerated from 145% in Q2 to 45% in Q3, attributed to the end of "token maxing."
  * *Lack of Moats:* Easy for customers to switch models, forcing Anthropic to cut prices by 50% in October to defend market share against cheaper open-weight models.
  * *Balance Sheet & Cost Risks:* Anthropic has $900B in commitments, meaning it will have to raise expensive debt (a junk credit rating is possible) while spending heavily to keep its frontier models competitive.
* **Mailbag 1 — Correction vs. Bear Market Positioning:** A correction lasts 1–2 years; a true bear market lasts years (none since the 1970s). The US economy is too dynamic and banks are too well-capitalized for a long-term bear market.
  * *Long-term investors:* Dollar-cost average into the S&P 500 index and ignore the noise.
  * *Traders:* Rotate into a healthcare index, a staples index, and short-term Treasuries.
* **Mailbag 2 — Identifying "Liar Loans" in 2008:** Moody’s securitization database revealed that starting in 2006, ~50% of all securitized subprime loans were "low doc" or "no doc" loans. Underwriters actively cajoled borrowers into overstating income (e.g., telling a $40,000 earner they needed to state $50,000 to qualify), though the exact percentage of liar loans within low-doc pools remains unknown.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* "The Jensen unwind is just starting, and it's going to get very ugly." — Steve Eisman
* "In the end, Nvidia's revenue is going to be lower. How much lower, we don't yet know. Maybe it can grow from there, but it has to go down first, I think." — Steve Eisman
* "It's going to be several quarters before we know how much Nvidia's business model will be negatively impacted." — Steve Eisman
* "There is no sign, no sign, that the housing market will improve anytime soon." — Steve Eisman
* "I don't foresee a long-term bear market because the US economy is more dynamic than perhaps anytime in its history... The US will recover." — Steve Eisman
* "We're spending $750 to $800 billion of CapEx in 2026 going to a trillion next year [2027]. In 2030, to justify all those numbers... our economy [has] to spend in aggregate per year $2.4 to $3 trillion a year." — Steve Eisman (referencing his Substack interview with Gary Gensler)

## Notable Quotes
> "Without Nvidia backstopping the AI stack, AI is no longer one trade, and that's why stock picking is back, and valuation is back." — Steve Eisman

> "The lesson here is that a bad macro trumps a good company almost every time." — Steve Eisman (on Home Depot)

> "Anthropic is a business with slowing revenue growth, increasing expenses and increasing cost of capital. I just think there are too many risks here and that's why I am uninvolved." — Steve Eisman

items.title: Learn 90% of charisma in under 60 minutes
items.summary: Charisma is a learnable skill—not an innate trait—rooted in balancing warmth and competence (which together drive 82% of first impressions) to trigger oxytocin and dopamine in others.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR**
Charisma is a learnable skill—not an innate trait—rooted in balancing warmth and competence (which together drive 82% of first impressions) to trigger oxytocin and dopamine in others. By using purposeful body language, vocal confidence, playful conversational hooks, and strategic mirroring, leaders and professionals can build immediate trust and influence without faking authenticity.

---

## The Science of Charisma: Warmth, Competence, and Brain Chemistry
* **Warmth as a Lubricant for Competence:** Vanessa Van Edwards notes that warmth and competence make up 82% of our impressions of people. Smart professionals often over-index on competence, which backfires because competence without warmth breeds suspicion.
  * Warmth is not "bubbly extroversion" or fake smiling; it shows up as vulnerability, humor, sarcasm, or even stumbling with words (e.g., Elon Musk’s unpolished vulnerability or Mark Zuckerberg’s everyday-guy demeanor).
* **Rejecting "Just Be Yourself":** Both Sam Parr and Vanessa agree that "authenticity" and "just be yourself" are unhelpful advice for people trying to improve. Instead, charisma is about honing your own distinct flavor of communication.
* **The First-Minute Rule:** First impressions are nearly irreversible; your first minute matters more than your first 30 minutes because the primitive brain is assessing friend vs. foe.
  * **Oxytocin (Connection):** Triggered in the first 3–5 seconds of eye contact, visible open hands (signaling no hidden weapons), and physical touch. A handshake produces roughly 3 hours' worth of eye-contact oxytocin.
  * **Dopamine (Motivation & Energy):** Triggered verbally by breaking social scripts and creating "information gaps" (e.g., Sam opening the show with a magic trick his daughter taught him, or Howard Stern asking, "Want to hear the weirdest thing that ever happened to me?"). Vanessa advises using information hooks every 1–2 minutes when speaking.

## Mastering Conversation: Hooks, Small Talk, and Playfulness
* **Entertainers vs. Appreciators:** Vanessa challenges Dale Carnegie’s advice to just ask lots of follow-up questions. While *Entertainers* love being the center of attention and answering questions, most VIPs are *Appreciators* who spend all day talking and want to be entertained or hear your stories.
  * Sam shares a story of dining with a ~$30 billion AI pioneer who spent the entire dinner asking Sam about his basic AI use cases because he was tired of being interviewed himself.
* **Dr. Dan McAdams’s Three Levels of Connection:**
  * **Level 1 (General Traits):** Basic facts ("What do you do?"). Vanessa recommends swapping this for, *"Working on anything exciting these days?"*—a question she honed over 20 years.
  * **Level 2 (Personal Concerns):** Motivations, values, and goals. Transition here quickly by asking about goals tied to time boxes (quarters, New Year's, birthdays) or what someone is learning (e.g., books).
  * **Level 3 (Self-Narrative):** The story someone tells themselves about themselves.
* **Playfulness and Trigger Words:** Keep a mental list of 20–50 "trigger words" (topics you enjoy) to steer conversations. Halting boring small talk with playful guessing games (e.g., guessing where someone is going on vacation or joking about baby names) triggers dopamine for both parties without requiring loud extroversion.
* **Being "Chalant":** Sam and Vanessa emphasize that enthusiasm—the physical display of passion—is contagious. Citing a dating study by Monica Moore, Vanessa notes that availability signals make people more attractive than physical looks alone, both romantically and professionally.

## Vocal Confidence, Language, and Leadership
* **Contagious Emotions & "Calm Assertive" Leadership:** Vanessa cites an fMRI study where participants smelled sweat from skydivers and "caught" their fear in their amygdala. Sam connects this to his experience at age 21 training an 80-pound pit bull ("Jake's dog"), where he learned that leaders must be *calm assertive* rather than high-energy reactive.
* **Eliminating Uptalk:** Using an accidental question inflection at the end of statements (e.g., stating a $10,000 price like a question) signals nervousness and deception, switching the listener's brain from listening to scrutinizing.
  * Men often do this in the first 10 seconds of a call/meeting while trying to sound warm; women often do it during the most nerve-wracking parts of a pitch.
* **Maximum Resonance Point:** Every voice has a 10-to-12-note range. Speaking on the out-breath at the lower, relaxed end of your range projects confidence—without overcorrecting to an unnatural extreme.
* **Purposeful Language (Behavior Cues):** In a prisoner’s dilemma study, groups told they were playing the "Wall Street game" shared an average of 1/3 of their profits, while groups told they were playing the "Community game" shared 2/3. Leaders should audit their sent emails and intentionally use achievement words (*win, succeed, master*) for performance days and collaborative words for brainstorming days.

## Reading People, Hiring, and Mirroring VIPs
* **Hiring "Ambitious Heroes":** Vanessa looks for candidates whose self-narrative is overcoming hurdles through grit.
  * **Behavioral & Hypothetical Questions:** Ask about the *most recent* hurdle they overcame (so it’s unrehearsed) or give them a real-time logistical hypothetical.
  * **The Luck Test:** Sam asks candidates, *"Do you feel lucky?"* Vanessa confirms research shows people who feel unlucky feel out of control and literally spot fewer opportunities.
  * **The Character Question:** From 10 years of research (Question #7 of 9 in her book), Vanessa asks: *"What book, movie, or TV character is most like you?"*—and warns never to argue with their answer, as it reveals how they predictably operate.
* **Finding Your Flavor:** Rather than mimicking one celebrity, watch the top 10–20 TED Talks to see which delivery style resonates with you.
* **Mirroring VIPs:** To charm high-status individuals without seeming like a clown (and with good, non-manipulative intent), mirror them on three planes:
  * **Non-verbally:** Match their animation, gestures, and pause lengths (e.g., matching a "2-second pauser").
  * **Verbally:** Adopt their exact lexicon (e.g., saying "clients" instead of "customers" if they do).
  * **Tonally:** Match their volume and speaking speed.

## Vanessa Van Edwards’s Business Model & Growth
* **Milestones & Scale:** Vanessa started posting YouTube videos every week in 2007. Today, her company has 10 employees, generated 300 million views last year, and recently hit the *New York Times* bestseller list (a 20-year goal).
* **Revenue Streams:**
  * **Corporate Speaking & Consulting:** Her largest revenue bucket.
  * **Courses & Teaching:** Flagship course *People School* (office hours and workshops for leaders), LinkedIn Learning, MasterClass, and teaching a full-credit course at Harvard.
  * **Book Royalties & Social Sponsors.**
  * **Corporate Certification:** Certifying internal HR and tech staff to act as in-house communication coaches.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Corporate Certification Growth:** Vanessa predicts that certifying internal communication coaches inside companies will be the primary focus and driver of her business over the next 5 years.
* **The "CCO" Ambition:** Vanessa’s long-term bet is that—especially as AI reshapes communication—companies and schools will adopt her curriculum and install a certified Chief Communication Officer (CCO) or Chief Conversation Officer in every organization.

## Notable Quotes
> "Competence without warmth is likely to leave us feeling suspicious. Not unlikeable, suspicious." — Vanessa Van Edwards

> "Likability is a lubricant for your smarts." — Vanessa Van Edwards

> "I think that human beings don't realize that we're just animals, and that all this primitive stuff is true." — Sam Parr

> "I think it's more exhausting to not get your ideas and not get what you want... than the alternative." — Vanessa Van Edwards

items.title: Obituaries | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
items.summary: Jensen Huang’s November 12, 2026 resignation as CEO of Nvidia—nominally triggered by personal affairs—marks the end of an era of tech company independence, as the U.S. government now treats AI hardware makers like defense contractors and banks rather than commercial businesses.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** Jensen Huang’s November 12, 2026 resignation as CEO of Nvidia—nominally triggered by personal affairs—marks the end of an era of tech company independence, as the U.S. government now treats AI hardware makers like defense contractors and banks rather than commercial businesses. Without Huang’s singular leadership, Nvidia’s structural moats, supply chain relationships, and debt-fueled "neocloud" ecosystem face severe vulnerability.

## The Fall of Jensen Huang and Nvidia's "Exoskeleton"
* **The Resignation:** Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on Thursday, November 12, 2026, ending a 33-year tenure that began when he co-founded the company on April 5, 1993.
* **Nominal vs. True Cause:** 
  * Nominally, Huang stepped down due to affairs with at least two Nvidia employees and Alice Huang, an executive at Singaporean data center firm MegaSpeed (who is alleged to be a Chinese spy).
  * Fundamentally, Huang’s exit was caused by his refusal to accept that Nvidia was now viewed by Washington as a defense contractor. 
* **The "Exoskeleton" Structure:** Nvidia was uniquely organized around one man, operating like a startup with very little middle management, 60 direct reports to Huang, and no succession plan. While this enabled rapid, aggressive bets, it left no internal checks on Huang's behavior or compliance.
* **The Asian Supply Chain:** Huang acted as a "one-person coordination function" for the Asian supply chain, famously eating and drinking across Asia to convince reluctant suppliers to commit capacity to Nvidia’s yearly release cycle.

## The Erosion of Nvidia's Four Moats
* **Historical Dominance:** Nvidia’s rise was built on the 2001 GeForce 3 (programmable pixel shaders), the 2006 launch of CUDA (an API that almost killed the company before becoming its core platform), and the 2019 acquisition of Mellanox (enabling scale-out systems). Following ChatGPT’s 2022 launch, Nvidia commanded margins exceeding 70%.
* **Moat 1 — CUDA (Eroding):**
  * Developer energy has moved up the stack to LLM APIs, making CUDA less relevant for most companies.
  * Anthropic proved leading LLMs can eliminate Nvidia dependency by learning to run on Amazon’s Trainium chips and Google’s TPUs.
  * LLMs themselves are so effective at writing software that any software-based moat will inevitably dry up.
* **Moat 2 — Networking & Systems (Challenged):** While more durable than CUDA, Nvidia's systems approach is increasingly challenged by Google and Anthropic, and relies heavily on neoclouds that struggle with power access and political permission.
* **Moat 3 — Supply Chain Mastery (Tenuous):** Huang bragged that he never signed a contract with TSMC over their three-decade partnership, relying instead on a handshake and mutual trust. Without Huang, that commitment is in question.
* **Moat 4 — Organizational Speed (Collapsed):** With Huang gone, the single-founder exoskeleton that allowed Nvidia to outmaneuver rivals is poised to collapse.

## The AI Bubble (2025–2027) and Nvidia's "Risky Business"
* **Shifting Funding Mechanisms:** The AI infrastructure build-out progressed from hyperscaler free cash flow, to debt (second half of 2025), and now to equity (starting with Google in summer 2026).
* **The Neocloud Hedge:** To avoid complete dependence on hyperscalers (who are building their own chips), Nvidia aggressively sold to "neoclouds" (independent GPU renters). 
* **Circular Financing:** Because neoclouds face expensive debt and increasingly worthless equity, Nvidia used its own cash flow and credit rating to backstop and fund its own customers.
* **The $1 Trillion Threshold:** Industry-wide AI revenue of roughly $1 trillion needs to materialize sooner rather than later. If it falls short, hyperscalers will prioritize their own compute, and Nvidia’s neocloud hedge will turn into a millstone, flooding the market with distressed assets.

## AI as "Normal Technology" vs. China Hawks and Doomers
* **The Policy Battle:** Huang argued AI was "normal technology" with engineering-solvable safety issues, putting him at odds with both AI "doomers" (e.g., Anthropic) and "China hawks," who viewed him as public enemy number one.
* **The China Dilemma:** China traditionally accounted for roughly 25% of Nvidia’s sales. When the Biden administration imposed chip controls in 2022, Nvidia immediately released the A800 (an A100 with a third of its interconnects disabled), establishing a pattern of abiding by the letter—never the spirit—of the law.
* **The "Great Firewall" Playbook:** China is currently banning imports of Nvidia’s two-generations-behind H20 chips (after the Trump administration banned and then reversed the ban). By cutting off access to Nvidia, China is forcing domestic demand to use inferior local alternatives—the exact strategy used with the Great Firewall to build Chinese internet giants—which will eventually enable a competing Chinese semiconductor ecosystem.

## The End of Tech Company Independence (1968–2026)
* **The Intel Precedent:** Since Robert Noyce founded Intel in 1968 (backed by Arthur Rock), tech companies operated on the premise that the world was their customer, volume drove progress, and executives—not the government—defined their products.
* **The Banking Standard:** In a *Financial Times* interview, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent demanded answers from Nvidia’s board and outside counsel within 10 days and called for a "shake-up" with an external CEO. 
* **Compliance Over Ignorance:** Bessent criticized Howard Lutnick’s Commerce Department for delaying adding MegaSpeed to the U.S. blacklist, but argued Nvidia should be held to the same standard as a bank: ignorance is not a defense, and companies must put "boots on the ground" to enforce the spirit of U.S. sanctions.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **The U.S. Chip Ecosystem:** Because "doomers and hawks have won" and AI will not be treated as normal technology, "in the fullness of time, it is the U.S. chip ecosystem that will pay the ultimate price." — *Ben Thompson*
* **Chinese Alternatives:** By forcing internal demand onto domestic chips, China's homegrown alternatives and supporting semiconductor ecosystem "will flood the world" in the long run. — *Ben Thompson*
* **Neoclouds & Nvidia's Exoskeleton:** Absent Huang’s willingness to shore up the ecosystem, Nvidia's neocloud hedge "is liable to turn into a millstone," and Nvidia's founder-centric exoskeleton "is much more poised to collapse than you might expect." — *Ben Thompson*

## Notable Quotes
> "Huang’s exit, nominally because of affairs with a buyer who may or may not have been a Chinese spy, as well as at least two company employees, was ultimately because Nvidia was, by the powers that be, considered a defense contractor and Huang never adjusted." — *Ben Thompson*

> "If Nvidia 'were a bank and they hadn't complied like this, the Treasury's Office of the Comptroller of the Currency would be in there right now and a lot of the executives would be removed.'" — *Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent*

> "When AI was deemed to be anything but normal, however, business as usual wasn't just over. It was a crime, and it cost Huang his job, and maybe more." — *Ben Thompson*

> "It makes it even more imperative that we sprint in the opposite direction of China towards more freedom and a bet on inventing new industries, not more control and a focus on gatekeeping what we have." — *Ben Thompson*

items.title: President Trump News Conference
items.summary: Following a four-day trip to Asia that culminated in the first-ever trilateral summit between the United States, Russia, and China, President Donald Trump touted a series of major trade deals, a trilateral nuclear risk-reduction declaration, and domestic permitting reform, while facing ongoing domestic debate over the Iran conflict and recent tech outages.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR**
Following a four-day trip to Asia that culminated in the first-ever trilateral summit between the United States, Russia, and China, President Donald Trump touted a series of major trade deals, a trilateral nuclear risk-reduction declaration, and domestic permitting reform, while facing ongoing domestic debate over the Iran conflict and recent tech outages.

---

## Historic Asia Trip & US-Russia-China Trilateral Summit
* **First-Ever Trilateral Summit:** President Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a historic trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, signing a first-of-its-kind peace declaration stating that nuclear conflict must never occur.
  * **Nuclear Balance:** Trump noted the three nations hold 92% of the world's nuclear power, estimating the U.S. has 4,000 nuclear weapons and China has 600. China agreed for the first time to conduct trilateral discussions on reducing nuclear risk.
  * **Energy & ICC:** The three leaders agreed to work together to increase oil, gasoline, and diesel production, and China joined in condemning the International Criminal Court (ICC).
  * **Diplomatic Rationale:** Secretary of State Marco Rubio emphasized that regular engagement among the three largest nuclear powers is essential, arguing it sets a positive foundation for trade negotiations and global safety.
* **Skeptical Assessment of China-Russia Ties:** Prior to the press conference, former National Security Adviser John Bolton warned that Xi and Putin have formed a "partnership without limits" where China is the dominant partner, creating a tri-polar nuclear world for which the U.S. lacks a strategy.
* **Ukraine & Bilateral Meetings:** Trump stated that Putin expressed a desire to end the Russia-Ukraine war diplomatically, noting that 25,000 soldiers are being killed every month. Trump also met with Xi on economic progress, noting fentanyl coming into the U.S. by sea is down 97%.

## Trade Deals, Tariffs & Economic Metrics
* **Southeast Asia & ASEAN Deals:** At the ASEAN summit in Manila, Trump secured more than $17 billion in commercial deals, including:
  * **Philippines:** Philippine Airlines will purchase 20 Boeing 787 Dreamliners with General Electric engines (supporting 47,000 U.S. jobs). The Philippines also agreed to buy 100% of its agricultural products (starting January 1) and 100% of its energy from the U.S., alongside more than $2 billion in U.S. military equipment.
  * **Thailand:** Signed an agreement to eliminate all tariffs and non-tariff barriers on U.S. products and purchase $2.6 billion per year in U.S. agricultural goods.
* **North American Trade:** Trump noted he is close to a deal with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum on trade surpluses and cartels, while criticizing Canada over an $80 billion U.S. trade deficit.
* **Domestic Economic Claims:** Trump highlighted 10 straight months of manufacturing growth, a 21% increase in new equipment investment, $25 trillion in new wealth created since taking office (though $4 trillion was lost after the election), and record-low poverty.
  * **Auto Manufacturing:** Trump cited new U.S. investments driven by tariffs, including a $4 billion Audi plant, a $5 billion Toyota plant, and the expansion of a Detroit Ford plant originally built in 1906.
  * **Energy Prices:** Crude oil has dropped 20% since early November to nearly $80 a barrel, and gasoline is down 60 cents a gallon from a month ago.

## Super Intelligence (SI), Data Centers & Domestic Permitting
* **Global AI/SI Competition:** Trump stated the U.S. leads China in "Super Intelligence" (SI) and agreed with Xi to establish joint guardrails. The U.S. also launched a Quad SI Accelerator with India, Australia, and Japan.
* **Ban on Overseas Data Centers:** Trump announced that the U.S. will not allow American companies to build data centers in other countries (citing a proposed facility in Finland), threatening "tremendous" taxes and penalties to keep construction—and energy infrastructure—domestic.
  * He noted local communities are benefiting financially, citing deals in Louisiana paying teachers $50,000 and another area giving residents $10,000 apiece.
* **Permitting Reform:** The Senate passed a bipartisan permitting reform bill that Vice President JD Vance said will enable unprecedented domestic construction of homes, factories, and power plants. Trump projected the bill will put at least $1,300 a year back into Americans' pockets.

## Iran Conflict, Oil Blockade & War Powers Debate
* **Senate War Powers Vote:** For the 15th time, Senate Republicans blocked a War Powers resolution to end hostilities in Iran, failing 48–51. GOP Senators Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, and Rand Paul joined most Democrats in favor, while Democrat John Fetterman and Republican Tom Tillis voted against.
  * **Opposition View:** Sen. Tim Kaine (D-VA) argued the war is unconstitutional and violates the 1973 War Powers Act's 60-day limit, calling the November 3 election results a repudiation of the conflict.
* **Administration Stance:** Trump stated Iran "will never have a nuclear weapon, ever," and noted the U.S. Navy's blockade gives the U.S. total control over the Strait of Hormuz, allowing record amounts of oil to move out. Vice President Vance argued on Fox News that the U.S. has destroyed Iran's nuclear program and conventional military.
* **Bolton's Critique:** John Bolton argued that while the U.S.-Israeli strikes and oil blockade have devastated Iran's economy and leadership, Trump lacks a clear, long-term strategy for regime change and failed to coordinate with NATO, Gulf Arab states, or Asian allies before the strikes began.

## Domestic Issues & Tech Outages
* **System Outages:** Addressing public concern over recent banking, credit card, and air traffic control outages, Trump said the incidents—such as Chase and other companies going down—are separate events caused by thousands of companies simultaneously upgrading their systems, not a coordinated crisis.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **China's Nuclear Catch-Up:** "China is way behind, but they'll catch us within 10 years, they're going at it hot and heavy." — *President Donald Trump*
* **Permitting Reform Savings:** The bipartisan permitting reform bill, if passed by the House, is "projected to put at least $1,300 a year back in the pockets of hardworking Americans." — *President Donald Trump*
* **Philippines Agricultural Purchases:** The Philippines will "buy 100% of your agriculture from January 1st from our farmers." — *President Donald Trump*
* **Quad Business Forum:** The top businesses from the U.S., India, Australia, and Japan "are going to meet early next year under the auspices of the President's sponsorship... and hopefully come up with additional commercial agreements." — *Secretary of State Marco Rubio*
* **Iran Regime Change:** "The most likely outcome in the near term would be that the existing regime disintegrates... and in the near term, you end up with some kind of military government, not led by the Revolutionary Guard, but by the regular military." — *John Bolton*

---

## Notable Quotes
> "These three countries, the United States, Russia and China, between these three countries possess the overwhelming majority of nuclear weapons on this planet. The idea that these three leaders should not engage on a regular basis is not just absurd, it's dangerous."
> — *Secretary of State Marco Rubio*

> "I think what's really going on here is that there's a Chinese-Russian axis emerging. It may look a lot like the Sino-Soviet alliance of the Cold War, but actually, in this incarnation, it's China that's dominant, China really calling the shots."
> — *John Bolton, Former National Security Adviser*

> "More than anything, I think the President has done, and not just his second term, but his first term as well, is that he's reorganized the global economy so that it makes sense to invest in the United States of America again."
> — *Vice President JD Vance*

> "Whoever wins SI wins, remember that. Whoever wins SI wins and you want to take advantage of the data centers... we're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country."
> — *President Donald Trump*

items.title: Trump Threatens to Tax Firms Building Data Centers Abroad: Full Presser
items.summary: Following a four-day Asia trip that included a historic trilateral summit with China's President Xi Jinping and Russia's President Vladimir Putin, President Donald Trump announced plans to heavily tax U.S. companies that build data centers abroad, detailed over $17 billion in new Pacific trade deals, and pushed for a $50 billion overhaul of the U.S. air traffic control system.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** Following a four-day Asia trip that included a historic trilateral summit with China's President Xi Jinping and Russia's President Vladimir Putin, President Donald Trump announced plans to heavily tax U.S. companies that build data centers abroad, detailed over $17 billion in new Pacific trade deals, and pushed for a $50 billion overhaul of the U.S. air traffic control system.

## Asia Trip, Trilateral Summit & Global Security
* **First-Ever US-Russia-China Trilateral Summit:** President Trump met with President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, focusing on nuclear de-escalation among the three nations, which hold 92% of the world's nuclear weapons (Trump noted the U.S. has ~4,000, Russia is second, and China has 600).
  * The three leaders signed a formal trilateral peace declaration stating nuclear conflict must never happen, with China agreeing for the first time to trilateral nuclear risk discussions and to condemn the International Criminal Court (ICC).
  * Secretary of State Marco Rubio emphasized that regular engagement among the three nuclear powers is essential to set a conducive tone for diplomacy and global safety.
  * The three nations also agreed to increase oil, gasoline, and diesel production to lower global prices.
* **Russia-Ukraine & Iran:** Trump stated Putin wants to end the war in Ukraine diplomatically, noting an average of 25,933 people (mostly soldiers) are dying monthly, though animosity between Putin and President Zelenskyy remains a major hurdle. Regarding Iran, Trump stated the U.S. Navy has a blockade in the Hormuz Strait, took out record amounts of oil last week, and vowed Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.
* **Historic Travel & Regional Positioning:** Air Force One completed a record 14.5-hour non-stop flight home without refueling (4 hours short of the previous record, compared to a typical 20-hour flight). Trump also noted the U.S. secured Greenland (thanking Denmark and NATO's Mark Rutte) and boxed China and Russia out of Venezuela and the Panama Canal.

## Trade Deals & International Partnerships
* **ASEAN & Philippines ($17B+ in Deals):** Addressing 14 ASEAN nations in Manila, Trump secured over $17 billion in commercial deals, including Philippine Airlines purchasing 20 Boeing 787 Dreamliners with General Electric engines (supporting 47,000 U.S. jobs).
  * The Philippines and Malaysia agreed to use U.S. cloud infrastructure.
  * Starting January 1, the Philippines will buy 100% of its agricultural products and 100% of its energy from the U.S., alongside over $2 billion in U.S. military equipment, under a framework deal slashing Philippine tariffs.
* **Thailand:** Signed an agreement to eliminate all tariffs and non-tariff barriers on U.S. products and purchase $2.6 billion per year in U.S. agricultural goods.
* **Quad Summit (US, India, Australia, Japan):** Launched the Quad Bureau leaders forum (meeting early next year), a Quad Super Intelligence (SI) accelerator, and new maritime security and surveillance collaborations.
* **China, Mexico & Canada:** Trump said the U.S. is negotiating a "comprehensive" deal with China, noting previous tariffs reached 145% plus a 20% fentanyl penalty (fentanyl entering by sea is down 97%). He is also working with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum on trade surpluses and cartels, and pressing Canada over an $80 billion trade deficit despite Prime Minister Carney's interest in building the Keystone pipeline.

## Data Centers, AI & Tech Policy
* **Tax Threat on Foreign Data Centers:** Trump announced plans to impose a "tremendous tax" and penalties on U.S. companies that build data centers in other countries (such as Finland) to prevent China from dominating the sector.
  * He urged communities in states like Texas, California, and West Virginia to welcome data centers, noting they generate their own electricity and offer local payouts—citing examples of companies paying teachers $50,000 in Louisiana and residents $10,000 each for project approvals.
* **Chips & Nvidia:** Trump stated the U.S. is 10 years ahead of China in chipmaking and will only allow older chips—not the latest **Blackwell** chips—to be sold to China. He praised former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as "brilliant" and said he would like to see Huang apologize and return to Nvidia.
* **AI Leadership:** Trump noted Anthropic's recent successful launch, expressed respect for CEO Dario Amodei, and said he and President Xi agreed to establish joint guardrails on "super intelligence."

## U.S. Economy, Infrastructure & Domestic Agenda
* **Economic Metrics & Manufacturing:** Trump reported creating $25 trillion in new wealth in under two years (though $4 trillion was lost post-election), 10 straight months of manufacturing growth, a 21% increase in new equipment investment, and record-low poverty.
  * Crude oil is down 20% since November to ~$80/barrel, and gasoline is down 60 cents/gallon in the past month.
  * Trump criticized the Federal Reserve as "very political," arguing lower interest rates (where each point equals $650 billion) could push U.S. GDP from 4% to 14–20%.
  * **Industrial Expansion:** Audi ($4 billion plant), Toyota ($5 billion plant), GM, and Ford are expanding U.S. operations, including a 1906 Detroit Ford plant now running 24/7. Defense contractors are also building 21 plants for Patriots, Tomahawks, and THAAD systems.
* **Permitting Reform & ATC Overhaul:** Vice President JD Vance highlighted the Senate's passage of bipartisan permitting reform legislation, which Trump said is projected to put at least $1,300/year back into Americans' pockets. Trump also requested $50 billion from Congress (up from $12 billion) to replace the 55-year-old air traffic control system under a single primary contractor like Raytheon or IBM.
* **Crime, Border & Bipartisan Bills:** Trump reported zero illegal border crossings in 18 months, murders at a 125-year low, and crime down 87% in Washington, D.C. and 81% in Memphis. He expressed openness to working with Democrats on healthcare, immigration, a federal film/TV production bill, and an NCAA/NIL college sports bill (noting colleges are losing up to $500 million/year).
* **Administration Backing:** Trump affirmed confidence in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, citing tens of billions made on Intel stock. Chief of Staff Stephen Miller touted 10-to-1 net deregulation, ending DEI, record fossil fuel/coal production, and defeating 20%+ year-over-year inflation.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Economic & Legislative Impact:** The bipartisan permitting reform bill, if passed by the House, is projected to put at least $1,300 per year back into the pockets of hardworking Americans — *President Donald Trump*.
* **Nuclear Parity:** China is currently behind the U.S. and Russia with 600 nuclear weapons, but will catch up to the U.S. within 10 years — *President Donald Trump*.
* **Chip Obsolescence:** Nvidia's latest Blackwell chips will be obsolete in two years — *President Donald Trump*.
* **College Sports:** Every college in the country will go bankrupt if Congress does not pass an NIL/college sports reform bill — *President Donald Trump*.
* **Administration Outlook:** Under President Trump's leadership, the next two years are going to be the greatest two years in American history — *Chief of Staff Stephen Miller*.

## Notable Quotes
> "We're not going to allow companies to build data centers in other countries. If they do that, they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them if they do it." — *President Donald Trump*

> "The idea that these three leaders [the U.S., Russia, and China] should not engage on a regular basis is not just absurd, it's dangerous." — *Secretary of State Marco Rubio*

> "More than anything, I think the President has done... is that he's reorganized the global economy so that it makes sense to invest in the United States of America again." — *Vice President JD Vance*

> "The first President in American history to achieve net deregulation. In other words, not only were more regulations removed than added, but 10 to 1, for every new one, 10 regulations removed." — *Chief of Staff Stephen Miller*

items.title: Why AI Has DHH Working 16-Hour Days
items.summary: David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH) argues that the agent era has reopened the operating system market for the first time in 25 years, making Linux—whose terminal, config files, and detailed error messages are ideal for AI—the natural successor to macOS and Windows.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR**
David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH) argues that the agent era has reopened the operating system market for the first time in 25 years, making Linux—whose terminal, config files, and detailed error messages are ideal for AI—the natural successor to macOS and Windows. Through his agent-first Linux distribution, Omarchy, DHH demonstrates how tiny teams can now rival tech giants, while taste, craft, and the obsession over the "final 2%" remain the true differentiators.

## The Agent-First OS Opportunity: Why Linux Wins Now
* **The End of Mouse-and-Click OSs:** DHH, who spent 30 years building software (Basecamp v5, Ruby on Rails v8, Hey.com) and used Mac since OS X Beta 4 in 2001, switched to Ubuntu 2.5 years ago over Apple’s 30% App Store cut and developer hostility. He argues macOS and Windows are fundamentally unfit for agents, whereas Linux’s historic weaknesses—heavy terminal use, text config files, and verbose error messages—are the exact interfaces agents love.
* **Omarchy’s Rapid Rise:** Built part-time in ~2.5 months by DHH and Ryan Hughes, Omarchy is designed to be modified live by prompting. DHH has not written a single line of code by hand in 5–6 months, instead generating hundreds of thousands of lines via agents. The Omarchy Foundation has raised ~$23M in tokens and donations.
* **Breaking Platform Lock-In:** 
  * **Desktop & Mobile:** Apple risks becoming the "AOL of the agent era" with walled gardens and features like Genmoji. DHH’s motto is *"first we take Manhattan (desktop), then we take Berlin (mobile)."*
  * **Eradicating App Moats:** An Omarchy community member replicated Adobe Lightroom in two weeks—a feat that took Adobe ~15 years and tens of millions of dollars. DHH no longer uses Word or Photoshop, relying on agents to draft contracts, generate PDFs, sign documents, and edit photos.
  * **Anish Acharya’s Take:** Five years ago, building a third mobile ecosystem was certain to fail due to app availability; today, a modest token budget can replicate the top 10,000 apps, or agents can simply perform the work natively without the app.

## The Economics of Software, Speed, and the Final 2%
* **Token Velocity & Model Leaps:** Current models run at ~50 tokens/sec (120 on ultra-fast), but Fireworks recently demonstrated 1,500 tokens/sec—generating a playable Tetris game in 4 seconds and mutating a side-scroller shooter live. During Omarchy’s development, models jumped from Opus 48 to Saul to Opus 55.
* **Negligible Cost:** Despite having the means for unlimited compute, DHH only uses three Claude subscriptions—and mostly relies on a single $200 20x subscription, maxing it out only two weeks out of the last three months.
* **Craftsmanship & Taste Still Matter:** Martin Casado noted that great software—like *StarCraft* receiving a Ghost balance patch after 20 years—is defined by long-tail design choices rather than raw lines of code. DHH agreed, explaining he is working 16-hour days because agents eliminate the friction of fixing the "final 2%," where he gets his dopamine.
* **Hyperdrive Without Headcount:** Basecamp/37signals has ~60 employees; DHH never wanted 6,000 or 60,000. Agents provide the productive capacity of 60,000 people with zero HR or coordination overhead—echoing Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke’s description of returning to a 7,000-person office as "coming out of hyperdrive."

## Superintelligence, Frontier Labs vs. Open Weights
* **Software vs. Hardware Timelines:** DHH believes we already have superintelligence for software development. However, Martin Casado’s personal AGI test—giving models a $20,000 budget to order parts and build an autonomous, walkable robot—shows physical embodiment is far behind (his setup, Groqbot, mostly orders home automation gear). Visiting Unitree in China two weeks prior, DHH found robotics engineers projecting 4–10 years for embodied breakthroughs, contrasting with Silicon Valley’s 1-year timelines.
* **Avoiding a Frontier Duopoly:** Drawing parallels to the 1990s encryption wars and Google/Meta capturing 99% of online ad value, DHH warned against a commercial or government-enforced duopoly between top labs (Anthropic and OpenAI). 
* **The Role of Open Weights:** DHH cheers on US frontier labs (including xAI and Google) while stressing that open-weight models (e.g., GLM 53, DeepSeek Flash, which he estimates are ~6–7 months behind) keep pricing honest. Local models like Qwen 3 8 Flash/Next now run usefully on a single-digit-thousand-dollar DGX Spark on a desk.

## The Return of Hacker, Demo, and Pseudo-Anonymous Culture
* **Industry Veterans & Empathy:** Martin Casado and Anish Acharya highlighted how stalwarts like DHH, Eric Raymond, John Carmack, Tim Sweeney, and Mitchell Hashimoto are guiding the industry. While DHH expressed empathy for anxious programmers—comparing them to 1970s Detroit auto workers and English Luddites—he insisted there is no going back.
* **Pseudo-Anonymous Builders:** Agents are redemocratizing software, bringing back 1990s hacker culture. The Omarchy core team and Foundation sponsor pseudo-anonymous contributors like Outfoxed (creator of QuickShell), Handcore, 0x0, and MiasLab, connected largely via X.
* **90s Demo & BBS Nostalgia:** Rejecting Jony Ive’s "aluminum-polished" aesthetic that stripped character from computers, Omarchy embraces 1995 demo-party vibes with a 40-effect ASCII screensaver and ASCII loading animations. DHH reminisced about running an illegal 3-line BBS out of his bedroom at age 14 on a US Robotics 33.6k modem, arguing computers should feel mysterious and cool again.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Unseating macOS:** Omarchy/Linux will surpass macOS’s 180 million users within 3 years—and potentially within 12 months, though DHH wouldn't put majority odds on the 1-year mark. *(DHH)*
* **True Superintelligence:** It is "entirely possible" that true superintelligence—better than humans at everything, including polishing a bespoke Linux kernel—arrives by next year. *(DHH)*
* **Macroeconomic Impact:** Widespread adoption of current agentic workflows puts annual GDP acceleration of 3%, 4%, 5%, or even 10% within the realm of possibility. *(DHH)*
* **Embodied Robotics:** Physical, actuator-driven AI breakthroughs are likely 4, 5, or 10 years away rather than imminent. *(Unitree engineers, relayed by DHH)*

## Notable Quotes
> "Every single thing that made Linux hard to use in the past—oh, it's very terminal heavy, it's got a bunch of config files that's hard to figure out, and it's got inscrutable error messages—these are the three things agents love." — David Heinemeier Hansson

> "Anyone who still thinks that there is moat in source code, even millions of lines of it, or that that is going to protect their ecosystem are delusional." — David Heinemeier Hansson

> "For whatever reason, I am blessed with the entire dopamine payoff in the last 2%. I don't actually give a fuck about the first 98." — David Heinemeier Hansson

> "Computers should be a little mysterious, they should be a lot of cool, and they should not be so polished... We're fucking getting the hackers back." — David Heinemeier Hansson

items.title: Anthropic Goes Public After Record-Breaking IPO | Bloomberg Tech
items.summary: Anthropic made history on the Nasdaq (ticker: ANTH) as the largest IPO of all time and the first pure-play Frontier AI lab to go public, raising $107.3 billion at $83 a share before opening at $111.50—a ~34% premium valuing the company at roughly $2 trillion.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Anthropic made history on the Nasdaq (ticker: ANTH) as the largest IPO of all time and the first pure-play Frontier AI lab to go public, raising $107.3 billion at $83 a share before opening at $111.50—a ~34% premium valuing the company at roughly $2 trillion. Investors and executives framed the listing not as a finish line, but as "day one" for deploying a massive $232 billion cash war chest into enterprise AI diffusion and next-generation compute.

## The Record-Breaking Debut & Market Backdrop
*   **Historic Scale & Pricing:** Host Ed Ludlow detailed that Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, raising $107.3 billion (including a $26 billion private placement largely backed by hyperscalers and strategics). Lead underwriters Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley orchestrated the opening trade, which walked up from $102–$103 indications to open at $111.50 per share (~$2 trillion fully diluted valuation) before settling around $106–$108.
    *   The offering was roughly 7x oversubscribed, with about 13% allocated to retail investors (compared to ~25% for SpaceX).
*   **Nasdaq’s Banner Year:** Nasdaq President Nelson Griggs noted that Anthropic caps a historic five-month stretch featuring the three largest IPOs in history: SpaceX (June), SK Hynix, and Anthropic. 
    *   Nasdaq has captured 91% of 2026 operating company IPO proceeds to date and added over $4 trillion in market cap via transfers, including GM this week.
    *   Griggs noted that the average 2026 IPO is up ~16% versus the broader market's 15%, with value stocks outperforming growth stocks this year.
*   **Mixed Broader Markets:** Bloomberg’s Isabelle Lee reported volatile trading alongside the debut. The Nasdaq swung from +2.5% pre-market into negative territory before hovering up 0.1% to 0.7%, while the S&P 500 flirted with a six-day losing streak (its longest since April 2024).
    *   **Semiconductors:** The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 1.5%–2%. Nvidia gained 1.5% (snapping a five-day losing streak following strong Tuesday earnings), Broadcom rose 1.5%, and AMD fell 6% (after dropping as much as 11%) due to a short-seller report.
    *   Investors remain watchful of AI capex ROI and potential regulatory headwinds for data center buildouts following a "blue sweep" in the recent midterm elections.

## Anthropic’s Financial Engine & Compute Strategy
*   **Hyper-Growth Trajectory:** Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao highlighted that the company is not yet six years old (founded 2021) and earned its first dollar of revenue in Q1 2023, yet surpassed $81 billion in run-rate revenue last month.
    *   Altimeter Partner Pauline Yang noted that since the start of 2025, Anthropic's revenue is up 45x while compute costs are up only 10x. Compute fell from 10x revenue in 2023 to 55% of revenue in H1 2026, tracking toward a long-term steady-state target of 45%–50%.
*   **Fortress Balance Sheet:** Rao confirmed Anthropic entered the IPO with over $130 billion in cash and now holds roughly $232 billion in cash and short-term investments.
*   **Multi-Silicon & "Anthropic Direct":** To manage what Rao called the "cone of uncertainty" around future model capabilities and demand, Anthropic uses a diversified compute strategy across four different accelerator platforms. Beyond buying from cloud partners, its "Anthropic Direct" strategy involves leasing data centers and chips separately to maintain fungibility and resilience.

## Investor Perspectives: Growth, Diffusion & Enterprise Focus
*   **From Passing to Doubling Down:** Altimeter’s Pauline Yang revealed the firm passed on Anthropic’s early 2023 ($4 billion) and subsequent rounds due to negative gross margins (2023–2024) and questions over its commercialization DNA. Altimeter first invested 18 months ago in the $180 billion round, co-led its $65 billion raise in May, and secured a public-fund allocation in the IPO.
    *   Yang attributed recent revenue surges to specific model releases: Opus 4.5 (late 2025) turned "vibe coding into production code," and Opus 55 added $10 billion in ARR in October alone.
*   **"Bigger, Faster" vs. "Private for Longer":** Baillie Gifford Head of Private Companies Peter Singlehurst—whose firm first invested in August 2025 across Series F, G, and H—contrasted SpaceX (24 years to IPO) with Anthropic (6 years to IPO), noting Anthropic created two decades' worth of value in six months.
*   **The Enterprise & Diffusion Thesis:** Both investors emphasized that Anthropic’s focus on enterprise (coding, law, healthcare, biotech, robotics) offers far higher ROI and pricing power than consumer markets, where free models suffice.
    *   Singlehurst highlighted **diffusion** as a massive secondary growth driver alongside new model capabilities: Fortune 500 aggregate spend on Anthropic currently represents just 0.1% of their total spend, leaving vast room for expansion.

## Governance, Safety & The Public-Market Balancing Act
*   **Public Benefit Corp (PBC) Dynamics:** Both Rao and Singlehurst pushed back on the idea of an inherent tension between Anthropic’s AI safety mission and shareholder returns. Singlehurst argued that pursuing safe AI is "completely compatible with maximizing long-term shareholder value."
*   **Political & Commercial Conviction:** At the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei stated Anthropic "will not bend to business or political pressure." Yang praised management's conviction—citing their willingness to hold their ground during earlier friction with the Department of War—and noted that all seven co-founders remain at the company with industry-leading retention.
*   **Expected Volatility:** Yang cautioned that Anthropic will likely be a volatile stock quarter-to-quarter because revenue spikes around major model releases while compute capacity comes online in non-linear chunks.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
*   **Revenue Growth Normalization:** Anthropic’s revenue growth will slow from the 10x pace seen in Q3 to closer to 2.5x next year, supported by underlying customer data — *Pauline Yang, Altimeter*.
*   **Cybersecurity as a 2027 Catalyst:** Cybersecurity ("cyber") will be a major revenue driver for Anthropic in 2027 as enterprises deploy AI to identify and patch code vulnerabilities — *Pauline Yang, Altimeter*.
*   **Multi-Trillion Dollar AI Winners:** The expanding AI total addressable market will support more than one $5 trillion to $10 trillion company over time, including both Anthropic and OpenAI — *Pauline Yang, Altimeter*.
*   **OpenAI IPO Timeline:** OpenAI will follow Anthropic into the public markets "soon" to secure the balance sheet required for capital-intensive AI execution — *Pauline Yang, Altimeter*.
*   **IPO Pipeline:** There will be a handful of IPOs in the two clear weeks of December before year-end, followed by a "rich and diverse pipeline for 2027" including power-generating companies tied to the AI buildout — *Nelson Griggs, Nasdaq*.

## Notable Quotes
> "If you look back, the company's not even six years old, right? And the first dollar of revenue in the business was Q1 of 2023. And since that time you flash forward not that long to last month where we had over $81 billion of run rate revenue."
> — Krishna Rao, CFO of Anthropic

> "There's nothing normal about this year. You get to the size of these IPOs, it's truly historic."
> — Nelson Griggs, President of Nasdaq

> "We think that there's going to be more than one winner that can generate a 5 to 10 trillion dollar company over the fullness of time, and we certainly think Anthropic and OpenAI are both in that category."
> — Pauline Yang, Partner at Altimeter

> "This isn't 'private for longer.' This is 'bigger, faster.' The value that's being created here is on par with value created over two decades and it's happened in six months."
> — Peter Singlehurst, Head of Private Companies at Baillie Gifford

items.title: Anthropic Makes Historic Debut on Nasdaq
items.summary: Anthropic (ticker: ANT) made history on the Nasdaq as the first pure-play frontier AI lab to go public and the largest IPO of all time, pricing at $83 per share, opening at $111.50 (a ~33–34% premium and ~$2 trillion valuation), and raising $107.3 billion.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR**
Anthropic (ticker: ANT) made history on the Nasdaq as the first pure-play frontier AI lab to go public and the largest IPO of all time, pricing at $83 per share, opening at $111.50 (a ~33–34% premium and ~$2 trillion valuation), and raising $107.3 billion. Backed by a ~$232 billion post-IPO cash war chest and $81 billion in run-rate revenue, executives and major investors framed the listing as "day one" for enterprise AI diffusion, even as broader equity markets fluctuated on AI capex ROI concerns.

## The Historic Nasdaq Debut & Deal Mechanics
* **Record-Breaking Deal Size:** Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share and raised $107.3 billion (which CFO Krishna Rao noted could be nearer to $120 billion in total), including a $26 billion private placement largely backed by hyperscalers and strategic investors.
  * The offering was nearly 7x oversubscribed, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley serving as lead underwriters (Morgan Stanley orchestrated the opening cross).
  * Shares opened at $111.50—a 33–34% premium—putting Anthropic at a fully diluted valuation of roughly $2 trillion before settling around $106–$108.
* **Retail & Market Structure:** Nasdaq President Nelson Griggs noted that ~13% of Anthropic's IPO went to retail investors, compared to ~25% for SpaceX.
* **Nasdaq's Banner Year:** Griggs highlighted that Nasdaq has captured 91% of 2026 operating company IPO proceeds, buoyed by transfers like GM this week (bringing over $4 trillion in market cap to the exchange).
  * The last five months have seen the three largest IPOs in history: SpaceX (June), SK Hynix, and Anthropic.
  * Average 2026 IPOs are up ~16% versus 15% for the broader market, though Griggs noted a "pretty slow fall" due to market volatility and the midterm election cycle, with only two clear IPO weeks remaining in December.

## Financial Performance, Compute Strategy & Balance Sheet
* **Hyper-Growth Trajectory:** CFO Krishna Rao emphasized that Anthropic is under six years old and generated its first dollar of revenue in Q1 2023, scaling to over $81 billion in run-rate revenue last month.
  * Since the start of 2025, revenue has grown 45x while compute costs grew 10x.
  * Compute and infrastructure costs fell from 10x revenue in 2023 to 55% of revenue in the first half of this year, with a long-term steady-state target of 45–50%.
* **Fortress Balance Sheet:** Entering the IPO with over $130 billion in cash and raising ~$120 billion, Anthropic now holds roughly $232 billion in cash and short-term investments.
* **"Anthropic Direct" & Diversified Compute:** Rao explained that Anthropic manages a "cone of uncertainty" around future model capabilities and demand by maintaining a diversified, fungible compute fleet across four different accelerator platforms.
  * Alongside cloud partners, the company is increasingly using **Anthropic Direct**—leasing data centers and chips separately—and is positioned to opportunistically acquire distressed cloud or data center assets if needed.

## Investor Perspectives: Growth, Diffusion & Enterprise Focus
* **Altimeter's Conviction (Pauline Yang):** Altimeter, which helped lead Anthropic's $65 billion raise in May and first invested at the $180 billion round (after passing on the early 2023 $4 billion round due to gross margin concerns), requested a $5 billion IPO allocation for its public fund and plans to hold long-term.
  * Yang noted that model releases drive step-function revenue spikes—such as Opus 3.5 adding $10 billion in October ARR, and Opus 4.5 (late 2025) turning "vibe coding" into production code.
  * She highlighted that all seven co-founders remain at Anthropic, giving it the best talent retention in the industry.
* **Baillie Gifford's "Bigger, Faster" Thesis (Peter Singlehurst):** Baillie Gifford first invested in August 2025 (Series F, G, and H) and views Anthropic as an outlier that broke the 15-year "private for longer" trend (SpaceX took 24 years to go public vs. 6 years for Anthropic).
  * Singlehurst emphasized **diffusion**—distributing existing frontier intelligence across industries—as a massive growth driver alongside new model releases, noting that Anthropic currently captures just 0.1% of aggregate Fortune 500 spend.
  * Both Yang and Singlehurst stressed that Anthropic's enterprise focus (coding, cybersecurity, law, healthcare, biotech, robotics) offers far greater pricing power and ROI than consumer AI, and both see room for multiple $5–$10 trillion winners, including OpenAI.

## Governance, Safety & Market Backdrop
* **Public Benefit Corp & Safety:** Anthropic's S-1 acknowledges existential AI risks and notes that safety safeguards may impact commercial growth. Both Yang and Singlehurst argued there is no long-term tension between safety and shareholder value, praising CEO Dario Amodei's conviction—including holding firm during an earlier entanglement with the Department of War—and noting that investors must accept that Anthropic may withhold models deemed too powerful.
* **Broader Market Volatility (Isabelle Lee):** The IPO occurred against a choppy market backdrop as investors questioned the ROI of massive AI infrastructure spending and the implications of a Democratic "blue sweep" on data center build-outs.
  * **Indices:** The Nasdaq swung from +2.5% pre-market into negative territory before hovering between +0.1% and +0.7%; the S&P 500 fell 0.3% (threatening its 6th straight loss, the longest streak since April 2024) before flipping to +0.1%.
  * **Semiconductors:** The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 1.5–2%. Nvidia gained 1.5% (snapping a 5-day losing streak post-earnings), Broadcom rose 1.5%, and AMD dropped 6% (after falling as much as 11% on a short-seller report).

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Growth Moderation:** Altimeter expects Anthropic's revenue growth to moderate from 10x (seen in Q3) to closer to 2.5x next year, supported by underlying customer data — *Pauline Yang, Partner at Altimeter*.
* **Cybersecurity as 2027 Catalyst:** Cybersecurity—specifically AI identifying and patching code vulnerabilities—will be a major revenue driver for Anthropic in 2027, followed by biotech and robotics — *Pauline Yang, Partner at Altimeter*.
* **Multi-Trillion-Dollar Winners:** The AI market will produce more than one $5 trillion to $10 trillion company over time, with both Anthropic and OpenAI in that category — *Pauline Yang, Partner at Altimeter*.
* **Stock Volatility:** Anthropic will be a "very volatile stock" quarter-to-quarter due to lumpy model releases, non-linear compute deliveries, and policy sensitivity, though trending up and to the right over the long term — *Pauline Yang, Partner at Altimeter*.
* **OpenAI & 2027 IPO Pipeline:** OpenAI will likely follow Anthropic to the public markets soon, while Nasdaq expects a rich, diverse 2027 IPO pipeline (including power-generating companies) once regulatory clarity on data center build-outs improves — *Pauline Yang (Altimeter) & Nelson Griggs (Nasdaq President)*.

## Notable Quotes
> "If you look back, the company's not even 6 years old, right? And the first dollar of revenue in the business was Q1 of 2023. And since that time, you flash forward not that long to last month, where we had over 81 billion dollars of run rate revenue." — **Krishna Rao**, Anthropic CFO

> "Six years from founding to public is an extreme. This isn't private for longer. This is bigger, faster. The value that's being created here is on par with value created over two decades, and it's happened in six months." — **Peter Singlehurst**, Head of Private Companies at Baillie Gifford

> "I think that this is truly day one, and I think that the team views this as a fundraising event really to continue to build their own journey." — **Pauline Yang**, Partner at Altimeter

> "There's nothing normal about this year. You get to the size of these IPOs, it's truly historic." — **Nelson Griggs**, President of the Nasdaq

items.title: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman: Inside the Largest Chip Ever Built | TomorrowX Summit
items.summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman set the record straight on its $20B+ OpenAI partnership—confirming sequential revenue growth and $200/watt token economics—while detailing how disaggregated inference (5x token output) and a dual hardware-cloud model will drive a major revenue and cash flow inflection in 2026–2028.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman set the record straight on its $20B+ OpenAI partnership—confirming sequential revenue growth and $200/watt token economics—while detailing how disaggregated inference (5x token output) and a dual hardware-cloud model will drive a major revenue and cash flow inflection in 2026–2028.

## OpenAI Partnership & Fast Token Economics
- **OpenAI Relationship Status:** Feldman dismissed social media rumors as misinformation, confirming OpenAI remains Cerebras's largest and most important customer.
  - Signed at the end of December 2025 ($20B+ contract; $25B in RPO noted by Gavin Baker), OpenAI revenue grew sequentially from Q2 to Q3, will grow again in Q4, and will continue growing throughout 2027.
- **$200/Watt Token Monetization:** Baker noted Wall Street often views $50–$60/watt ($50B–$60B/GW) as a revenue ceiling, but reports indicate OpenAI is selling Cerebras capacity to special customers for $200/watt ($200B/GW). Feldman confirmed, *"it's true."*
- **Hyperscaler Demand & Pricing Power:** Fast tokens on frontier models carry the highest gross margins because they are the most valuable to buyers.
  - Over the past six months, Cerebras signed **AWS, Microsoft, and Oracle** to resell fast tokens.
  - With power and space ~40% more expensive than in December 2025, new capacity is priced at a **40%–50% floor** above OpenAI's contract. Baker noted $25B in RPO would equate to $37B–$37.5B at today's prices, which Feldman said would be *"vastly higher."*

## Disaggregated Inference: 5x Data Center Output
- **Divide-and-Conquer Architecture:** Disaggregated inference splits workloads into **prefill** (processing the prompt) and **decode** (generating the answer). Using GPUs for prefill and Cerebras for decode generates **5x** as many tokens at the same speed from the same power footprint (e.g., a 10 MW data center).
- **Live Production & Universal Compatibility:** Cerebras has the world's first production deployment of disaggregated inference running with **AMD** on prefill and **Cerebras** on decode.
  - A software integration layer allows Cerebras to pair with any accelerator—including **NVIDIA GPUs, AWS Trainium, and ARM GPUs**—enabling retrofits into existing brownfield GPU data centers as well as greenfield sites.
- **Addressable Market:** Baker highlighted that if Cerebras were not supply-limited and attached to even 10% of accelerators in 3–4 years, it would represent tens of billions in revenue; Feldman stated Cerebras could attach to *"most"* GPUs/accelerators for inference.

## Wafer-Scale Architecture & Product Roadmap
- **First-Principles Bet:** Rather than making incremental GPU tweaks, Cerebras started with a clean sheet in late 2015/early 2016 to build the largest chip in compute history—**56x larger** than any prior chip—using **SRAM** instead of HBM/DRAM.
  - Baker noted this optimizes for memory bandwidth in a way that is uniquely hard to replicate, giving Cerebras a **15x–30x** (10x–30x) speed advantage in inference by getting weights to compute faster.
- **Three Consecutive Doublings:**
  - **CS4:** Just starting to ship; **2x** as fast as CS3.
  - **CS5:** Ships in summer; **2x** as fast as CS4.
  - **CS6:** Ships in summer 2028; at least **2x** as fast as CS5.

## Dual Business Model: Cloud vs. Hardware Cash Flow
- **Supply Chain & Q4/Q1 Ramp:** Following the December 25, 2025 OpenAI deal, Feldman flew to Taiwan to secure increased forecasts from TSMC and Cerebras's top 10–15 vendors, with new chips arriving in May/June. Data center delays pushed Q3 capacity into Q4 and Q1.
  - Baker noted Q4 revenue is up ~40% sequentially at the midpoint, and Feldman expressed *"high hopes"* for a similar uptick in Q1.
- **Cloud vs. Hardware Trade-offs:**
  - **Cloud:** Provides multi-year backlog and recurring revenue, but is capital-intensive with a 16–18 month payback period on gear.
  - **Hardware:** Lumpy (starts at zero each quarter) and requires customers to have their own data centers, but delivers immediate revenue recognition and strong cash flow.
- **Hyperscaler Hardware Deployments:** **Oracle, AWS, and Microsoft** will deploy Cerebras hardware in their own data centers, with the Oracle opportunity **more than double** AWS and Microsoft, beginning in **Q2 next year**.
  - Baker challenged the Street's consensus of a $2.5B cash burn next year given hardware's cash flow profile; Feldman confirmed hardware revenue will exceed cloud revenue in *"several"* quarters next year.

## Industry Perspective, Education & Community Impact
- **On Jensen Huang:** Feldman praised NVIDIA's CEO as *"the most successful CEO and the best CEO in the business"* over the last 15–20 years, calling his company-building *"the single most successful entrepreneurial act of my life."*
- **AI in Education:** Feldman highlighted that AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude can deliver free, individualized tutoring to any child—such as explaining long division 15 different ways—democratizing the elite model once reserved for figures like Alexander the Great (tutored by Aristotle).
- **Data Centers as Good Neighbors:** Though Cerebras is a data center tenant rather than a builder, Feldman said the company works transparently with local communities (such as a site two hours from Austin) to fund rounding-error community needs like high school football fields or 10 years of school power.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **OpenAI Revenue Growth:** OpenAI revenue will grow again in Q4 and continue growing throughout **2027** (Andrew Feldman).
- **CS5 & CS6 Roadmap:** CS5 will ship in **summer** at 2x CS4 speed, and CS6 will ship in **summer 2028** at least 2x CS5 speed (Andrew Feldman).
